sanskrit: tato duryodhanenāpi sabhrātrā samarodyataḥ pariṣvaktaḥ sthitaḥ karṇaḥ pragṛhya saśaraṃ dhanuḥ
english: Then Karṇa, embraced by Duryodhana along with his brothers who were ready for battle, stood there holding his bow with arrows set.

sanskrit: tataḥ savidyutstanitaiḥ sendrāyudhapurojavaiḥ āvṛtaṃ gaganaṃ meghair balākāpaṅktihāsibhiḥ
english: Then the sky became covered with clouds accompanied by lightning and thunder, preceded by Indra's bow, with lines of cranes laughing in their wake.

sanskrit: tataḥ snehād dharihayaṃ dṛṣṭvā raṅgāvalokinam bhāskaro 'py anayan nāśaṃ samīpopagatān ghanān
english: Then the Sun god, out of affection, seeing his son Karṇa gazing at the arena, drove away the clouds that had drawn near.

sanskrit: meghacchāyopagūḍhas tu tato 'dṛśyata pāṇḍavaḥ sūryātapaparikṣiptaḥ karṇo 'pi samadṛśyata
english: The Pāṇḍava then appeared hidden in cloud-shadow, while Karṇa, blazing in the light of the sun, was fully visible.

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrā yataḥ karṇas tasmin deśe vyavasthitāḥ bhāradvājaḥ kṛpo bhīṣmo yataḥ pārthas tato 'bhavan
english: The sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra stationed themselves where Karṇa stood; Droṇa son of Bharadvāja, Kṛpa, and Bhīṣma went to where Arjuna stood.

sanskrit: dvidhā raṅgaḥ samabhavat strīṇāṃ dvaidham ajāyata kuntibhojasutā mohaṃ vijñātārthā jagāma ha
english: The arena split into two sides; the women too were divided in heart. Kuntī, daughter of Kuntibhoja, understanding the situation, fell into a swoon.

sanskrit: tāṃ tathā mohasaṃpannāṃ viduraḥ sarvadharmavit kuntīm āśvāsayām āsa prokṣyādbhiś candanokṣitaiḥ
english: Vidura, who knew all duties, comforted Kuntī who had thus fainted, by sprinkling her with water mixed with sandalwood.

sanskrit: tataḥ pratyāgataprāṇā tāv ubhāv api daṃśitau putrau dṛṣṭvā susaṃtaptā nānvapadyata kiṃ cana
english: Then, having recovered her senses, she saw both sons clad in armor, and though deeply distressed, she could not do anything.

sanskrit: tāv udyatamahācāpau kṛpaḥ śāradvato 'bravīt dvandvayuddhasamācāre kuśalaḥ sarvadharmavit
english: When both had raised their great bows, Kṛpa the son of Śaradvat spoke — he who was skilled in the conduct of duels and knew all duties.

sanskrit: ayaṃ pṛthāyās tanayaḥ kanīyān pāṇḍunandanaḥ kauravo bhavatā sārdhaṃ dvandvayuddhaṃ kariṣyati
english: "This is the younger son of Pṛthā, the Pāṇḍava, a Kaurava — he will fight a duel with you.

sanskrit: tvam apy evaṃ mahābāho mātaraṃ pitaraṃ kulam kathayasva narendrāṇāṃ yeṣāṃ tvaṃ kulavardhanaḥ tato viditvā pārthas tvāṃ pratiyotsyati vā na vā
english: O mighty-armed one, do you likewise declare your mother, your father, and your lineage before these kings whose family you adorn — then, knowing who you are, Arjuna will decide whether to fight you or not."

sanskrit: evam uktasya karṇasya vrīḍāvanatam ānanam babhau varṣāmbubhiḥ klinnaṃ padmam āgalitaṃ yathā
english: The face of Karṇa, spoken to thus, drooped with shame and appeared like a lotus weighed down and dampened by raindrops.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca ācārya trividhā yonī rājñāṃ śāstraviniścaye tatkulīnaś ca śūraś ca senāṃ yaś ca prakarṣati
english: Duryodhana said: "O teacher, scripture establishes three types of origin for kings: one born of noble lineage, one who is a hero, and one who leads armies.

sanskrit: yady ayaṃ phalguno yuddhe nārājñā yoddhum icchati tasmād eṣo 'ṅgaviṣaye mayā rājye 'bhiṣicyate
english: If Phalguna does not wish to fight in battle with one who is not a king, then I shall consecrate this man as king over the realm of Aṅga."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas tasmin kṣaṇe karṇaḥ salājakusumair ghaṭaiḥ kāñcanaiḥ kāñcane pīṭhe mantravidbhir mahārathaḥ abhiṣikto 'ṅgarājye sa śriyā yukto mahābalaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, at that very moment, Karṇa the great chariot-warrior, endowed with glory and great strength, was consecrated as king of Aṅga by those who knew the sacred hymns, with golden pots adorned with flowers, upon a golden throne.

sanskrit: sacchatravālavyajano jayaśabdāntareṇa ca uvāca kauravaṃ rājā rājānaṃ taṃ vṛṣas tadā
english: Honored with white umbrella and fly-whisks, and amid shouts of victory, that king Karṇa — the bull among men — then spoke to that Kaurava king.

sanskrit: asya rājyapradānasya sadṛśaṃ kiṃ dadāni te prabrūhi rājaśārdūla kartā hy asmi tathā nṛpa atyantaṃ sakhyam icchāmīty āha taṃ sa suyodhanaḥ
english: "What shall I give you in return for this gift of a kingdom? Tell me, O tiger among kings, and I shall do it." Suyodhana replied to him: "I desire your undying friendship."

sanskrit: evam uktas tataḥ karṇas tatheti pratyabhāṣata harṣāc cobhau samāśliṣya parāṃ mudam avāpatuḥ
english: Thus spoken to, Karṇa replied "So be it," and both, embracing each other with joy, attained the highest delight.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ srastottarapaṭaḥ saprasvedaḥ savepathuḥ viveśādhiratho raṅgaṃ yaṣṭiprāṇo hvayann iva
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Adhiratha, the charioteer, with his upper garment slipping and trembling with perspiration, entered the arena, leaning on a staff, calling out as if summoning.

sanskrit: tam ālokya dhanus tyaktvā pitṛgauravayantritaḥ karṇo 'bhiṣekārdraśirāḥ śirasā samavandata
english: Seeing him, Karṇa, restrained by reverence for his father, laid down his bow, and with his head still wet from the consecration, bowed down at his feet.

sanskrit: tataḥ pādāv avacchādya paṭāntena sasaṃbhramaḥ putreti paripūrṇārtham abravīd rathasārathiḥ
english: Then, in great agitation, covering his feet with the hem of his garment, the charioteer called out with full feeling, "My son!"

sanskrit: pariṣvajya ca tasyātha mūrdhānaṃ snehaviklavaḥ aṅgarājyābhiṣekārdram aśrubhiḥ siṣice punaḥ
english: And embracing his head, overcome with affection, he wetted again with his tears the head that was still moist from the Aṅga kingdom consecration.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sūtaputro 'yam iti niścitya pāṇḍavaḥ bhīmasenas tadā vākyam abravīt prahasann iva
english: Seeing this, the Pāṇḍava Bhīmasena, having determined "this one is the son of a charioteer," then spoke these words, laughing as it were.

sanskrit: na tvam arhasi pārthena sūtaputra raṇe vadham kulasya sadṛśas tūrṇaṃ pratodo gṛhyatāṃ tvayā
english: "You, O son of a charioteer, do not deserve to be slain in battle by Arjuna. Act in keeping with your lineage — quickly take up the goad instead."

sanskrit: aṅgarājyaṃ ca nārhas tvam upabhoktuṃ narādhama śvā hutāśasamīpasthaṃ puroḍāśam ivādhvare
english: "You are not fit to enjoy the kingdom of Aṅga, O vile man — like a dog standing near the sacred fire claiming the sacrificial cake at a ritual."

sanskrit: evam uktas tataḥ karṇaḥ kiṃ cit prasphuritādharaḥ gaganasthaṃ viniḥśvasya divākaram udaikṣata
english: Thus addressed, Karṇa's lips quivered slightly; he sighed deeply and looked up at the Sun standing in the sky.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaḥ kopād utpapāta mahābalaḥ bhrātṛpadmavanāt tasmān madotkaṭa iva dvipaḥ
english: Then Duryodhana the mighty, in anger, sprang up from among that grove of brothers like an elephant maddened with rut.

sanskrit: so 'bravīd bhīmakarmāṇaṃ bhīmasenam avasthitam vṛkodara na yuktaṃ te vacanaṃ vaktum īdṛśam
english: He spoke to Bhīmasena of terrible deeds who stood there: "O Vṛkodara, it is not fitting for you to speak such words.

sanskrit: kṣatriyāṇāṃ balaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ yoddhavyaṃ kṣatrabandhunā śūrāṇāṃ ca nadīnāṃ ca prabhavā durvidāḥ kila
english: "Strength is the highest virtue among Kṣatriyas; one related to the warrior class must fight. The origins of heroes and of rivers are truly difficult to know.

sanskrit: salilād utthito vahnir yena vyāptaṃ carācaram dadhīcasyāsthito vajraṃ kṛtaṃ dānavasūdanam
english: "Fire arose from water and pervades all moving and unmoving things; from the bones of Dadhīci the thunderbolt was made, the slayer of demons.

sanskrit: āgneyaḥ kṛttikāputro raudro gāṅgeya ity api śrūyate bhagavān devaḥ sarvaguhyamayo guhaḥ
english: "The blessed god Guha is called the son of Fire, born of the Kṛttikās, son of Rudra, and son of the Gaṅgā — he who embodies all mysteries.

sanskrit: kṣatriyābhyaś ca ye jātā brāhmaṇās te ca viśrutāḥ ācāryaḥ kalaśāj jātaḥ śarastambād guruḥ kṛpaḥ bhavatāṃ ca yathā janma tad apy āgamitaṃ nṛpaiḥ
english: "Brahmins born of Kṣatriya women are also renowned; our teacher Droṇa was born from a pot; preceptor Kṛpa was born from a clump of reeds; and even the birth of your own family has been proclaimed by kings.

sanskrit: sakuṇḍalaṃ sakavacaṃ divyalakṣaṇalakṣitam katham ādityasaṃkāśaṃ mṛgī vyāghraṃ janiṣyati
english: "How could a doe give birth to a tiger like him, blazing like the sun, adorned with divine earrings and armor, and marked by celestial signs?

sanskrit: pṛthivīrājyam arho 'yaṃ nāṅgarājyaṃ nareśvaraḥ anena bāhuvīryeṇa mayā cājñānuvartinā
english: "This lord of men deserves the kingship of the whole earth, not merely Aṅga's kingdom — by virtue of this arm-strength of his and by my authority as his ally."

sanskrit: yasya vā manujasyedaṃ na kṣāntaṃ madviceṣṭitam ratham āruhya padbhyāṃ vā vināmayatu kārmukam
english: "Or whoever among men does not approve of what I have done — let him mount his chariot or stand on foot and bend his bow."

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvasya raṅgasya hāhākāro mahān abhūt sādhuvādānusaṃbaddhaḥ sūryaś cāstam upāgamat
english: Then a great cry of "Alas! Alas!" arose throughout the arena, accompanied by shouts of "Bravo!" — and the sun went to its setting.

sanskrit: tato duryodhanaḥ karṇam ālambyātha kare nṛpa dīpikāgnikṛtālokas tasmād raṅgād viniryayau
english: Then Duryodhana, O king, took Karṇa by the hand, and by the light of the torches they departed from that arena.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś ca sahadroṇāḥ sakṛpāś ca viśāṃ pate bhīṣmeṇa sahitāḥ sarve yayuḥ svaṃ svaṃ niveśanam
english: The Pāṇḍavas together with Droṇa and Kṛpa, O lord of men, and all along with Bhīṣma, departed each to his own quarters.

sanskrit: arjuneti janaḥ kaś cit kaś cit karṇeti bhārata kaś cid duryodhanety evaṃ bruvantaḥ prasthitās tadā
english: Some among the people departed crying "Arjuna!" some "Karṇa!" O Bhārata, and some "Duryodhana!" — so they went their ways.

sanskrit: kuntyāś ca pratyabhijñāya divyalakṣaṇasūcitam putram aṅgeśvaraṃ snehāc channā prītir avardhata
english: And in Kuntī's heart, love concealed by affection grew, for she had recognized her son the king of Aṅga, indicated by his divine marks.

sanskrit: duryodhanasyāpi tadā karṇam āsādya pārthiva bhayam arjunasāṃjātaṃ kṣipram antaradhīyata
english: And for Duryodhana too, O king, upon obtaining Karṇa, the fear that had arisen on account of Arjuna quickly vanished.

sanskrit: sa cāpi vīraḥ kṛtaśastraniśramaḥ; pareṇa sāmnābhyavadat suyodhanam yudhiṣṭhirasyāpy abhavat tadā matir; na karṇatulyo 'sti dhanurdharaḥ kṣitau
english: And that hero, having demonstrated his mastery of weapons, addressed Suyodhana with high courtesy; and Yudhiṣṭhira too formed the opinion at that time: "There is no bowman on this earth equal to Karṇa."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ śiṣyān samānīya ācāryārtham acodayat droṇaḥ sarvān aśeṣeṇa dakṣiṇārthaṃ mahīpate
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, having assembled all his students, Droṇa urged them all without exception to fetch his teacher's fee, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: pāñcālarājaṃ drupadaṃ gṛhītvā raṇamūrdhani paryānayata bhadraṃ vaḥ sā syāt paramadakṣiṇā
english: "Seize Drupada the king of Pāñcāla in the forefront of battle and bring him to me — that shall be your highest gift to me. May it go well with you."

sanskrit: tathety uktvā tu te sarve rathais tūrṇaṃ prahāriṇaḥ ācāryadhanadānārthaṃ droṇena sahitā yayuḥ
english: Saying "So be it," all of them, those mighty strikers, swiftly mounted their chariots and went together with Droṇa to give the teacher his fee.

sanskrit: tato 'bhijagmuḥ pāñcālān nighnantas te nararṣabhāḥ mamṛdus tasya nagaraṃ drupadasya mahaujasaḥ
english: Then those bulls among men attacked the Pāñcālas, slaying them as they went, and crushed the city of the mighty Drupada.

sanskrit: te yajñasenaṃ drupadaṃ gṛhītvā raṇamūrdhani upājahruḥ sahāmātyaṃ droṇāya bharatarṣabhāḥ
english: Those bulls of the Bhārata clan seized Drupada son of Yajñasena at the forefront of battle and brought him along with his ministers to Droṇa.

sanskrit: bhagnadarpaṃ hṛtadhanaṃ tathā ca vaśam āgatam sa vairaṃ manasā dhyātvā droṇo drupadam abravīt
english: His pride broken, his wealth taken, and now brought under subjection — Droṇa, reflecting on that old enmity in his mind, then spoke to Drupada.

sanskrit: pramṛdya tarasā rāṣṭraṃ puraṃ te mṛditaṃ mayā prāpya jīvan ripuvaśaṃ sakhipūrvaṃ kim iṣyate
english: "Your kingdom has been swiftly crushed and your city destroyed by me. Having fallen alive into the power of an enemy who was once your friend, what do you desire?"

sanskrit: evam uktvā prahasyainaṃ niścitya punar abravīt mā bhaiḥ prāṇabhayād rājan kṣamiṇo brāhmaṇā vayam
english: Having said this and laughed at him, Droṇa considered and then spoke again: "Do not fear for your life, O king — we Brahmins are forgiving.

sanskrit: āśrame krīḍitaṃ yat tu tvayā bālye mayā saha tena saṃvardhitaḥ snehas tvayā me kṣatriyarṣabha
english: "The affection that grew between you and me, O bull among Kṣatriyas, was nurtured by those childhood games we played together in the hermitage.

sanskrit: prārthayeyaṃ tvayā sakhyaṃ punar eva nararṣabha varaṃ dadāmi te rājan rājyasyārdham avāpnuhi
english: "I would seek friendship with you once again, O bull among men. I give you a boon, O king — receive back half of your kingdom."

sanskrit: arājā kila no rājñāṃ sakhā bhavitum arhati ataḥ prayatitaṃ rājye yajñasena mayā tava
english: "Indeed, one who is not a king cannot be the friend of kings. That is why I have striven for a kingdom of your own, O Yajñasena.

sanskrit: rājāsi dakṣiṇe kūle bhāgīrathyāham uttare sakhāyaṃ māṃ vijānīhi pāñcāla yadi manyase
english: "You are king on the southern bank of the Bhāgīrathī, and I am on the northern bank — know me as your friend, O Pāñcāla, if you are willing."

sanskrit: drupada uvāca anāścaryam idaṃ brahman vikrānteṣu mahātmasu prīye tvayāhaṃ tvattaś ca prītim icchāmi śāśvatīm
english: Drupada said: "This is not surprising, O Brahmin — among great souls of valor, such things occur. I am pleased with you and I desire an everlasting friendship with you."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu taṃ droṇo mokṣayām āsa bhārata satkṛtya cainaṃ prītātmā rājyārdhaṃ pratyapādayat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, Droṇa released him, O Bhārata, and honoring him with a glad heart, restored to him half the kingdom.

sanskrit: mākandīm atha gaṅgāyās tīre janapadāyutām so 'dhyāvasad dīnamanāḥ kāmpilyaṃ ca purottamam dakṣiṇāṃś caiva pāñcālān yāvac carmaṇvatī nadī
english: With a downcast heart, Drupada then settled in Makandi on the bank of the Gaṅgā, along with its dependent provinces, and in the great city of Kampilya, and over the southern Pāñcālas as far as the river Carmaṇvatī.

sanskrit: droṇena vairaṃ drupadaḥ saṃsmaran na śaśāma ha kṣātreṇa ca balenāsya nāpaśyat sa parājayam
english: But remembering his enmity with Droṇa, Drupada did not rest, and he saw no way to defeat him by Kṣatriya force alone.

sanskrit: hīnaṃ viditvā cātmānaṃ brāhmaṇena balena ca putrajanma parīpsan vai sa rājā tad adhārayat ahicchatraṃ ca viṣayaṃ droṇaḥ samabhipadyata
english: Knowing himself to be inferior in Brahminic power, that king resolved to seek the birth of a son — and Droṇa took possession of the territory of Ahicchattra.

sanskrit: evaṃ rājann ahicchatrā purī janapadāyutā yudhi nirjitya pārthena droṇāya pratipāditā
english: Thus, O king, was the city of Ahicchattra along with its surrounding provinces conquered in battle by Arjuna and delivered to Droṇa.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca prāṇādhikaṃ bhīmasenaṃ kṛtavidyaṃ dhanaṃjayam duryodhano lakṣayitva paryatapyata durmatiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Duryodhana the evil-minded, observing Bhīmasena who was superior in physical strength and Dhanañjaya who had mastered every science, burned with envy.

sanskrit: tato vaikartanaḥ karṇaḥ śakuniś cāpi saubalaḥ anekair abhyupāyais tāñ jighāṃsanti sma pāṇḍavān
english: Then Karṇa the son of Vikartana and Śakuni the son of Subala sought by many means to slay the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś cāpi tat sarvaṃ pratyajānann ariṃdamāḥ udbhāvanam akurvanto vidurasya mate sthitāḥ
english: But the Pāṇḍavas, those crushers of foes, were fully aware of all of this; making no outward show of it, they abided by the counsel of Vidura.

sanskrit: guṇaiḥ samuditān dṛṣṭvā paurāḥ pāṇḍusutāṃs tadā kathayanti sma saṃbhūya catvareṣu sabhāsu ca
english: The citizens, seeing the sons of Pāṇḍu full of virtues, would then gather and speak of them in the crossroads and assembly halls.

sanskrit: prajñācakṣur acakṣuṣṭvād dhṛtarāṣṭro janeśvaraḥ rājyam aprāptavān pūrvaṃ sa kathaṃ nṛpatir bhavet
english: "Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of men, uses wisdom as his eyes because of his blindness — he could not obtain the kingdom before; how then should he become king now?

sanskrit: tathā bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavaḥ satyasaṃdho mahāvrataḥ pratyākhyāya purā rājyaṃ nādya jātu grahīṣyati
english: "And Bhīṣma son of Shantanu, who is true to his word and bound by great vows, having renounced the kingdom long ago, will never take it up now.

sanskrit: te vayaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ taruṇaṃ vṛddhaśīlinam abhiṣiñcāma sādhv adya satyaṃ karuṇavedinam
english: "Let us therefore duly consecrate today the eldest Pāṇḍava, who is young in years yet old in conduct, truthful and compassionate."

sanskrit: sa hi bhīṣmaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ ca dharmavit saputraṃ vividhair bhogair yojayiṣyati pūjayan
english: "For he, knowing dharma, will honor and provide all manner of enjoyments to Bhīṣma son of Shantanu, to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and to their sons alike."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ duryodhanaḥ śrutvā tāni vākyāni bhāṣatām yudhiṣṭhirānuraktānāṃ paryatapyata durmatiḥ
english: Duryodhana the evil-minded, hearing those words of the citizens who were devoted to Yudhiṣṭhira, burned with anguish.

sanskrit: sa tapyamāno duṣṭātmā teṣāṃ vāco na cakṣame īrṣyayā cābhisaṃtapto dhṛtarāṣṭram upāgamat
english: That wicked soul, burning with envy, could not endure those words; scorched by jealousy, he came to Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: tato virahitaṃ dṛṣṭvā pitaraṃ pratipūjya saḥ paurānurāgasaṃtaptaḥ paścād idam abhāṣata
english: Then, finding his father alone and paying his respects, burning with the anguish of the citizens' affection for another, he afterwards spoke these words.

sanskrit: śrutā me jalpatāṃ tāta paurāṇām aśivā giraḥ tvām anādṛtya bhīṣmaṃ ca patim icchanti pāṇḍavam
english: "Father, I have heard the inauspicious words of the chattering citizens — setting you aside and Bhīṣma too, they wish the Pāṇḍava as their lord."

sanskrit: matam etac ca bhīṣmasya na sa rājyaṃ bubhūṣati asmākaṃ tu parāṃ pīḍāṃ cikīrṣanti pure janāḥ
english: "This is also Bhīṣma's view — he does not desire the kingdom; but the people of the city intend to inflict the greatest harm upon us."

sanskrit: pitṛtaḥ prāptavān rājyaṃ pāṇḍur ātmaguṇaiḥ purā tvam apy aguṇasaṃyogāt prāptaṃ rājyaṃ na labdhavān
english: "Pāṇḍu obtained the kingdom from his father and by his own virtues in former times; you too were given the kingdom but could not retain it due to the association of deficiencies."

sanskrit: sa eṣa pāṇḍor dāyādyaṃ yadi prāpnoti pāṇḍavaḥ tasya putro dhruvaṃ prāptas tasya tasyeti cāparaḥ
english: "If this Pāṇḍava obtains the heritage of Pāṇḍu, then it will go surely to his son and to his son's son, so others will say."

sanskrit: te vayaṃ rājavaṃśena hīnāḥ saha sutair api avajñātā bhaviṣyāmo lokasya jagatīpate
english: "We, deprived of the royal lineage along with our sons, shall become despised by the world, O lord of the earth."

sanskrit: satataṃ nirayaṃ prāptāḥ parapiṇḍopajīvinaḥ na bhavema yathā rājaṃs tathā śīghraṃ vidhīyatām
english: "So that we do not constantly fall into ruin and subsist on another's bounty, O king, make swift arrangements to prevent this."

sanskrit: abhaviṣyaḥ sthiro rājye yadi hi tvaṃ purā nṛpa dhruvaṃ prāpsyāma ca vayaṃ rājyam apy avaśe jane
english: "If only you had been firmly established in the kingdom from the start, O king, then we would have surely obtained the kingdom even if the people were unwilling."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dhṛtarāṣṭras tu putrasya śrutvā vacanam īdṛśam muhūrtam iva saṃcintya duryodhanam athābravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, having heard such words from his son, reflected for a moment and then spoke to Duryodhana.

sanskrit: dharmanityaḥ sadā pāṇḍur mamāsīt priyakṛd dhitaḥ sarveṣu jñātiṣu tathā mayi tv āsīd viśeṣataḥ
english: "Pāṇḍu was ever devoted to righteousness and always acted for my good and benefit; he was so to all the kinsmen, and especially so to me."
